decisions.rationale: number_to_currency has no static equivalent; /help does not ship until someone decides what it should render, so the target emits no page for it.
raw() output is unescaped author HTML from a Ruby expression; same route, same block.
the t() key resolves to nothing in this app's locale table; same route, same block.
broken.html.erb has an unclosed <% if %>; nothing can convert a template that does not parse, and nothing is emitted for it.
ghost_path names no route this run recovered; the link target is unknown, so /links does not ship.
legacy.html.haml is Haml; no converter reads that engine, so /posts/legacy is blocked rather than shipped empty.
/old keeps redirecting to /about; the host config owns the rule, so there is nothing for the static tree to carry.
the render call names its partial dynamically, so the index cannot be converted faithfully; Rails keeps serving /posts and this target emits no page for it.
@posts is request-time state; the list stays on Rails with the rest of /posts. Only the per-record page below moves, as a SPA.
/posts/:id is one page per record; a client-routed SPA mounted at /posts is the shape this converter can actually produce.
the sign-in form needs a session endpoint no static tree can offer; Rails keeps serving /session/new until Stage 3 binds the form to a backend operation.
the sign-up form stays on Rails on the same terms as the sign-in form.
the errors block only renders after a failed submit, which no static page can perform; it stays on Rails with the form it belongs to.

the full_messages loop inside that same errors block; retained with it. Its `|m|` block local is the region convert.zig cannot map, which is why this route also exercises ruling S19: the answer settles the route even so.
the @user ivar read that pre-fills the form; it has no meaning without the request that filled it, so it stays on Rails too.
